objective: Add one accessible, read-only robot-monitoring tab to the existing dependency-free Dashboard: render the Issue #170 health and history endpoints as one truthful overall status, severity-sorted active alerts, per-domain freshness cards and a bounded recent-trend table, with a single bounded refresh interval, backoff after failure, cancellation of superseded requests, and no state-changing control.
decision_supported: Can an operator see the current robot health and its active alerts in the shipped UI, and can that view be trusted not to show a stale or fabricated green status when data is missing, stale, alerting or unavailable?
acceptance: one monitoring tab presents a single truthful overall state and separate safety, power, CAN, compute, storage, localisation, motion, perception and task cards
every metric shows its unit, its reporting source and its freshness, and an explicit unknown or stale marker instead of a fabricated zero or a green status
active alerts are sorted by severity then age and show the metric, severity, observation count and an evidence reference
a bounded table shows the recent snapshots without adding a chart dependency
critical alerts remain visible at mobile widths and are announced through an accessible polite live region that updates only when the alert set changes
status is never carried by colour alone, and reduced-motion and forced-colors modes remain intact
a failed refresh clears the cards and reports monitoring as unavailable, so a stale green status cannot remain on screen
periodic refresh uses one bounded interval, cancels superseded requests, and pauses when the view or the page is hidden
a card defers to the backend alert rules, so a fresh reading that violates a threshold shows its alert severity rather than healthy
the view is strictly read-only and offers no acknowledge, reset, contactor, motion or STOP control
the fixture health document is visibly labelled a simulation fixture and its separate subdirectory keeps it from being parsed as a run log
evidence: Task Packet schema validation output with exit code
targeted pytest output listing the collected Issue #171 test names, pass counts and exit codes
a real headless-browser session at desktop and mobile widths showing the overall status, the alert list and the trend table with the reported console errors
screenshots for the healthy, degraded and recovered fixtures
a browser run proving a failed health request clears the cards instead of leaving a green status
mutation probe 1 output: with the alert-driven card status removed, the fresh-but-alerting test fails
mutation probe 2 output: with the missing/stale unknown mapping removed, the never-green-without-a-fresh-value test fails
mutation probe 3 output: with the failure-clears-payload line removed, the unavailable test fails
mutation probe 4 output: with the trend bound removed, the bounded-trend test fails
make test, make contract, make scenario-check, make golden-check, make context-check and make docs output with exit codes
final git diff --check and git diff --name-only output proving every changed path is allowed
stop_conditions: Meeting the acceptance requires changing the backend contract, the monitoring collector, an interface schema or a path owned by another module.
The view exposes an acknowledge, reset, contactor, motion or STOP control, or otherwise changes robot state.
A missing, stale or conflicting metric renders as healthy or as a fabricated zero.
A failed refresh leaves a stale green status on screen.
A chart library, frontend framework, WebSocket or browser notification dependency is added.
Polling becomes unbounded or continues while the view or the page is hidden.
data_classification: internal; the fixture is a synthetic simulation health document containing only registry metric names and values and no camera, prompt, recipient or credential data
model_policy: no model call; rendering, status derivation and polling are deterministic JavaScript
risks_and_fallbacks: A monitoring screen that shows a green card next to a red alert destroys trust in both. Card status is derived from the same backend alert set, so a fresh but threshold-violating metric renders at its alert severity.
Missing data rendered as a value is the classic false-green. A missing metric asserts no value and shows a word, never zero or false.
A failed refresh could leave the last good payload visible. The failure path clears the payload so the view can only report unavailable.
A five-second poll could spam a screen reader with the same announcement. The live region updates only when the alert signature changes.
A polling loop could keep running invisibly. Polling is scheduled only while the monitoring view is selected and the document is visible, and every superseded request is aborted.
A health document in the run-log directory would be parsed as a run and fail the read model. The fixture lives in a subdirectory and the default path was corrected with a regression test.
